
It does one thing. On a GitHub `pull_request.*` or `push` event, find the task from the branch name, or, when the branch does not resolve to a task, from a `Worklode-Task:` trailer in the pull request body; then read the `Spec:` trailer from the pull request body or the pushed commits, newest first. When it names a rule (`WL-REQ-<n>`) or a section (`WL-SPEC-75 sec-5`, resolved to the rule arranged at that anchor) and the task carries no `source = 'plan'` link, write a `governedBy` link with `source = 'gate'`. `none`, a missing or malformed trailer, an unknown task, an unknown target, a task already governed by a plan and an already gate-governed task are counted and change nothing. The `task.governed` event's external id, `spec-reconciler-<task id>-<declaration>`, names the link the trailer asks for, so redelivery and every later push carrying the same trailer for the same task collide with the first one and change nothing. The subscriber runs behind `SubscriberLock` beside `doc-lifecycle` and starts with it.
